intelligence.human_view: Think of a lighthouse with a town behind it. The light speaks to ships in their own language — signals, charts, codes — so they can find the harbor. Inside the town, everyone knows the square's colors: this street for market, this for the harbor office. The mayor's board shows everyone's standing where all can see it. And the town's highest honor isn't for the fastest runner — it's for the wisest citizen, the one who does right by everybody.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine walking through a beautiful shop where everything is already set up for you, and you just make each thing yours. Nobody in the shop reads your diary — your diary stays in your own special box that only you can open. And when we show someone our work, we show the real finished thing — not a drawing of it.
intelligence.grandma_view: A good shopkeeper lets the goods speak — you walk in, you see the real thing, you touch it, and by the counter you already know. And a trustworthy shopkeeper never reads the letters you leave in your box with her. She keeps the box locked and hands it back untouched. Presentation and discretion: that's the whole trade.
